rows.author: C020
rows.title_full: AN ACT ESTABLISHING A NATIONAL PROGRAM FOR FILIPINO GIFTED AND SCIENCE ORIENTED CHILDREN, PROVIDING FUNDS THEREFOR AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: This proposed measure aims to establish a national program for the Filipino gifted and science oriented children pursuant to the 1987 Constitution. A Center with its own Excutive Council shall be created to ensure the effective coordination and implementation of the said program with the objective of identifying the gifted and science oriented from ages 3 to 16; and providing them with development opportunities, scholarship grants and other forms of assistance to realize their full potentials.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on BASIC EDUCATION AND CULTURE since 2001-08-07

first_reading.comm_act: jt. ref'ls as per J.17; p.15 (Aug.28,20 01)

rows.author: C020
rows.mother_status: Approved by the House on 2002-09-03, transmitted to on 2002-09-03 and received by the Senate on 2002-09-03
rows.title_full: AN ACT CREATING THE DEPARTMENT OF HOUSING AND URBAN DEVELOPMENT, RATIONALIZING THE ORGANIZATION AND FUNCTIONS OF GOVERNMENT AGENCIES AND CORPORATIONS RELATED TO HOUSING AND URBAN DEVELOPMENT, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Among the objectives of this bill are: (1) to rationalize the structure, powers and functions of the different housing and urban development agencies; (2) to integrate all housing and urban development policies, plans, programs and projects o various government corporations and agencies to expedite delivery of decent, affordable and sustainable housing and urban development programs and projects to underprivileged and homeless citizens; and (3) to undertake a comprehensive and continuing program of urban development and housing which will make available at affordable cost decent housing and basic services to under privileged and homeless citizens.
rows.status: Substituted by HB04517

first_reading.comm_act: jt. ref'l as per J.37; p.19

rows.author: C020
rows.title_full: AN ACT GRANTING EXEMPTION TO THE MEMBERS OF THE JUDICIARY, INCLUDING THE CHIEF JUSTICE AND ASSOCIATE JUSTICES OF THE SUPREME COURT, AND THEIR PERSONNEL FROM THE COVERAGE OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 6758, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE SALARY STANDARDIZATION LAW
rows.abstract: This bill seeks to exempt from the coverage of RA 6758, otherwise known as the Salary Standardization Law, the members of the judiciary, including the Chief Justice and Associate Justices of the Supreme Court, and their personnel. It is in keeping with the declared policy of the State to provide equal pay for equal work that this bill is filed. It is also with the intention to keep the good men and women as well as to attract the best and the brightest in the Bench, which according to the latest data suffers from a vacancy reaching a staggering figure of over 700, that the early passage of this bill is earnestly sought.
rows.status: Substituted by HB05178

rows.author: C020
rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING ARTICLES 215 AND 216 OF THE LABOR CODE OF THE PHILIPPINES, AS AMENDED, BY UPGRADING THE SALARIES, ALLOWANCES AND RETIREMENT BENEFITS OF LABOR ARBITERS AND THE COMMISSIONERS OF THE NATIONAL LABOR RELATIONS COMMISSION (NLRC) AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Rationale: Since they perform an important part in the maintenance of industrial peace and in the adjudication of justice in the workplace, it is fitting that labor arbiters enjoy equality in rank with the judges of the RTC. Appropriate retirement benefits must likewise be accorded them to enable them to enjoy the fruits of government service long after they have been served it with their best years.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LABOR AND EMPLOYMENT since 2001-08-07

rows.author: C020
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROHIBITING THE PRESENTATION TO THE PRESS OR PUBLIC OF SUSPECTS IN CRIMINAL INVESTIGATIONS BEFORE CASES ARE FORMALLY FILED AGAINST THE SUSPECTS
rows.abstract: It shall be unlawful for any person to present publicly or in a press conference any suspect who is being investigated by a government office for possible criminal liability before formal charges are filed against him or her unless there is a written consent by the suspect with the assistance of a counsel. Anyone who has custody of the suspect cannot divulge the identity of the suspect in his or her custody prior to the filing of formal charges in court. > This bill, however, does not apply tosuspects who are at large or for whom warrants of arrest have been issud. Their names and photographs can be provided to the public for dissemination in order to facilitate their arrest.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on PUBLIC ORDER AND SECURITY since 2001-08-07

rows.author: C020
rows.title_full: AN ACT TO ESTABLISH A PROGRAM FOR THE ACQUISITION OF SCHOOL SITES AND THE CONSTRUCTION, MAINTENANCE, REHABILITATION, AND REPAIR OF PUBLIC ELEMENTARY AND SECONDARY SCHOOL BUILDINGS NATIONWIDE, APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: "School Building Program Act of 2001".  The bill seeks to create a comprehensive program which will address the problem of classroom shortage. A salient feature of this bill is the provision of build-operate-t ransfer, build-lease-tra nsfer, build-transfer, rehabilitate-o perate-transfer , and other contractural arrangements that will allow the use of both government and private funds to finance the construction of needed school buildings, and the creation of an inter-agency committee to formulate and ensure the effective implementation of the program by the Department of Education, Culture and Sports. The program also provide for the integration of all the necessary information for the effective monitoring and maintenance of existing schoool buildings.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on BASIC EDUCATION AND CULTURE since 2001-08-07

rows.author: C020
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE SUMMARY TITLING OF REAL PROPERTIES USED AS SITES FOR PUBLIC SCHOOLS
rows.abstract: Titles to real properties, public or private, including those owned or possessed by the national, provincial or municipal governments which are being utilized as actual sites for public schools for a period of at least five (5) years shall be transferred to the Department of Education, Culture and Sports by simple motion filed by the Office of the Solicitor General or Municipal, City or Provincial Prosecutor. The proceedings shall be summary in nature and the decision shall be final and executory and not subject to appeal except in a petition for certiorari to the Supreme Court.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on JUSTICE since 2001-08-07

rows.author: C020
rows.title_full: AN ACT EXEMPTING FROM TAX ALL ALLOWANCES AND BENEFITS GRANTED TO PUBLIC AND PRIVATE SCHOOL TEACHERS, INCLUDING THE FACULTY OF PUBLIC AND PRIVATE TERTIARY EDUCATION INSTITUTIONS
rows.abstract: "The Public and Private Schoolteachers' Tax Incentives Act."  All allowances and benefits granted to public and private schoolteachers, including the faculty of public and private tertiary education institutions, shall not be included in the computation of gross income and shall be exempt from taxation under Title III, Chapter VI of Republic Act No. 8424, otherwise known as the "Tax Reform Act of 1997".
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on WAYS AND MEANS since 2001-08-07

rows.author: C020
rows.title_full: AN ACT TO GRANT ADDITIONAL INSURANCE BENEFITS TO ALL PUBLIC SCHOOL TEACHERS, PROVIDING FUNDS FOR THE PAYMENT OF ITS PREMIUMS, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: In addition to the insurance benefits given to teachers by the Government Service Insurance System (GSIS) under Presidential Decree No. 1146, as amended, a term insurance coverage to all public schoolteachers providing the following benefits shall be granted: (1) P200,000.00 - death benefits; (2) P50,000.00 - burial expenses; (c) P100,000.00 - reimbursement of medical expenses.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on BASIC EDUCATION AND CULTURE since 2001-08-07

rows.author: C020
rows.title_full: AN ACT UPGRADING THE MINIMUM SALARY GRADE LEVEL OF PUBLIC SCHOOL TEACHERS IN THE ELEMENTARY AND SECONDARY LEVELS FROM GRADE 10 TO GRADE 18, GRANTING ADDITIONAL LONGEVITY PAY ADJUSTMENT EVERY FIVE YEARS AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Rationale: On public schoolteachers are overworked, underpaid and have become convenient menials for numerous non-teaching activities without hardly the proper recognition of their participation in such activities. The present compensation package for teachers is not adequate for basic family expenditures. While teachers are increasingly made to undertake activities beyond their normal teaching duties, their compensation does not increase to corresponding levels. Their economic status hardly improves.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on BASIC EDUCATION AND CULTURE since 2001-08-07

rows.author: C020
rows.title_full: AN ACT TO ASSURE MEANINGFUL DISCLOSURES OF THE TERMS OF RENTAL-PURCHASE AGREEMENTS, INCLUDING DISCLOSURES OF ALL COSTS TO CONSUMERS UNDER SUCH AGREEMENTS AND TO PROVIDE CERTAIN SUBSTANTIVE RIGHTS TO CONSUMERS UNDER SUCH AGREEMENTS
rows.abstract: Rationale: There is a significant number of consumers engage in rental-purchase transactions. Unfortunately, these transactions have taken place, in many instances, without adequate disclosures and other protections to consumers. > Hence, this billseeks to protect consumers by requiring meaningful disclosure of the terms of rental-purchase agreements and providing certain substantive rights to consumers who enter into rental-purchase agreements.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on TRADE AND INDUSTRY since 2001-08-07

rows.author: C020
rows.title_full: AN ACT TO PROVIDE FOR A SYSTEM OF ABSENTEE VOTING FOR QUALIFIED FILIPINOS ABROAD AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.abstract: All Filipinos abroad and dependents when residing with them who have all the qualifications and none of the disqualificatio ns of a voter, shall have the right to register and to vote by absentee system. They shall include the following: (1) Contract workers employed in foreign countries; (2) Employees of the Philippine Government assigned in foreign countries; (3) Filipino citizens who are legal immigrants or temporary residents of foreign countries; and (4) Member of the Armed Forces assignedto a foreign country.> For the first time that the system will be implemented, qualified Filipinos abroad shall vote in national elections only.
rows.status: Substituted by HB03570

first_reading.comm_act: jt. ref'l as per J.17; p.25(Aug. 28,2001)

rows.author: C020
rows.title_full: AN ACT GRANTING SPECIAL INCENTIVES TO PUBLIC PROSECUTORS IN ORDER TO ENCOURAGE THEM TO PERFORM THEIR DUTIES WELL, APPROPRIATING NECESSARY FUNDS THEREFOR AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: In recognition of their contribution in the fight against crime, state prosecutors, provincial prosecutors and city prosecutors of the DOJ and special prosecutors of the Office of the Ombudsman who successfully litigate criminal cases involving violation of the Revised Penal code in a full-blown trial court are hereby granted an incentive bonus of the One Thousand Pesos (P1,000.00) per case won if the work is completed within six (6) months from the date of arragement. > Those who are duly deputized by other government agencies, such as, but not limited to the Ofrfice of the Solicitor General and the Office of the Ombudsman shall be entitled to an allowance in the amount determined by the deputizing office: Provided, That the allowance tobe given by each deputizing office shall not exceed fifty percent (50%) of the basic pay of the prosecutors.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on JUSTICE since 2001-08-07

rows.author: C020
rows.title_full: AN ACT REQUIRING ADVERTISEMENT OF ALCOHOLIC BEVERAGES TO BEAR HEALTH WARNINGS
rows.abstract: "Sensible Advertising Act". Alcoholic beverages in the Philippines do not provide for healthy warning hence there is a significant need to fill the void. This bill addresses this need by providing specific health warnings in advertisements through magazine, newspapers, brochures, and promotional display as well as those made through radio, television, broadcasting or other electronic means.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on PUBLIC INFORMATION since 2001-08-07

rows.author: C020
rows.title_full: AN ACT PRESCRIBING THE CREATION AND FILLING UP OF ONE (1) MANDATORY POSITIONS OF BARANGAY NUTRITION WORKER IN EVERY BARANGAY PROVIDING INCENTIVES THERETO, APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE PD NO. 1569
rows.abstract: To strengthen the Barangay Nutrition Program, there shall be CREATED under the administration and SUPERVISION of the NATIONAL NUTRITION COUNCIL IN COORDINATION WITH THE CITY or MUNICIPALITY and the BARANGAY, ONE (1) MANDATORY POSITION OF BARANGAY NUTRITION WORKER IN EVERY BARANGAY WITH A MONTHLY ALLOWANCE OF NOT LESS THAN TWO THOUSAND PESOS (P2,000.00).
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on HEALTH since 2001-08-07

rows.author: C020
rows.title_full: AN ACT TO REQUIRE 90 DAYS NOTICE BEFORE CHANGING THE ANNUAL PERCENTAGE RATE OF INTEREST APPLICABLE ON ANY CREDIT CARD ACCOUNT OR BEFORE CHANGING THE INDEX USED TO DETERMINE SUCH RATE
rows.abstract: "Credit Card Internet Rate Charge Disclosure Act". Rationale: The state shall simplify, clarify and modernize the laws governing credit transactions and encourage the development of fair and economically sound-consumer credit practices. The state shall assure the full disclosure of the true cost of credit to protect the consumer from lack of awareness of the true cost of credit to the user.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on BANKS AND FINANCIAL INTERMEDIARIES since 2001-08-07

rows.author: C020
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROMOTING AND REGULATING THE OPERATION OF CABLE TELEVISION IN THE PHILIPPINES AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: "Cable Television Act of 2001". This bill provides incentives and support mechanisms that will promote competition in the field and allow a better-leveled comparative growth of the different players in the enterprise. The proposed legislation also seeks to rationalize government regulation of the industry be clearly delineating the powers of the government agency mandated by law.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on PUBLIC INFORMATION since 2001-08-07

rows.title_full: AN ACT DEFINING AND PUNISHING MONEY LAUNDERING AND PROVIDING FOR APPROPRIATE MECHANISMS FOR ITS DETECTION, PREVENTION AND PROSECUTION, INCLUDING THE CREATION OF THE NATIONAL ANTI-MONEY LAUNDERING BOARD, DEFINING THE POWERS AND FUNCTIONS THEREOF ANDAPPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: It is the policy of the State to ensure that criminals, organized crime groups, corrupt public officials and the proceeds of their unlawful activities cannot find safe haven in or use the Philippines as a money laundering site, offshore center or transit point and to extend strong cooperation in any transnational investigation, prosecution and extradition involving money laundering activities whereber committed.

rows.abstract: Significant provisions of this bill areas follows: (1) INCREASED fines for violation of banking laws from [P30,000.00] to P300,000.00 per banking day for each violation; and (2) establishment of a COMPENSATION PLAN for Bangko Sentral personnel.

rows.title_full: AN ACT AUTHORIZING BARANGAY OFFICIALS TO ACT MEDIATORS AND CONCILIATORS IN LABOR DISPUTES, PARTICULARLY WAGE CLAIMS OF LESS THAN FIVE THOUSAND PESOS (P5,000.00), PROVIDING FOR THE TRAINING OF THESE MEDIATORS AND CONCILIATORS, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSES THE LABOR CODE AS AMENDED, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: "Barangay Mediation and Conciliation Act of 2001". The Secretary of Labor is hereby authorized to deputize barangay officials to act as conciliators or mediators and help in the early settlement of disputes, actual or prospective, arising from labormanagement relations in companies located within the jurisdiction of said barangay officials. For this purpose, the Secretary of Labor shall train selected barangay officials on effective methods and techniques of conciliation and mediation, and with further training even act as voluntary arbiters, if so chosen by both parties.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LABOR AND EMPLOYMENT since 2001-08-07

rows.title_full: AN ACT REDUCING THE QUANTITIES OF PROHIBITED DRUGS AS A BASIS IN THE APPLICATION OF PENALTIES, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE THE DANGEROUS DRUGS ACT OF 1972, AS AMENDED
rows.abstract: The proposed amendment to the Dangerous Drugs Act of 1972 is as follows: "Section 20. Applications of Penalties Confiscation and Forfeiture of the proceeds for offenses under Sections 3, 4, 7, 8 and 9 of Article II and Sections 14, 14-A, 15 and 16 of Article III of this Act shall be applied if the dangerous drugs involved is in any of the following quantities: (1) [40] 20 grams or more of opium; (2) [40] 20 grams or more of morphine; (3) [200] 10 grams or more of shabu or methamphetamine hydrochloride; (4) [40] 20 grams or more of heroine; (5) [750] 350 grams or more of indian help or marijuana; (6) [50] 25 grams or more marijuana resin or marijuana resin oil; (7) [40] 20 grams or more of cocaine or cocaine hydrochloride.
rows.status: Substituted by HB04433

rows.title_full: AN ACT GRANTING SPECIAL BENEFITS TO GOVERNMENT PERSONNEL RETIRED UNDER R.A. 660, R.A. 1616, AND P.D. 1146, WHO ARE 70 YEARS OR OLDER, BY PROVIDING NEW PROCEDURES IN THE COMPUTATION OF MONTHLY PENSIONS AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Rationale: Despite the commendable adjustments of the GSIS with regard to the retirement benefits taht they give, it is sad to note that they still fall short of the expected outcome. As a result, retirees are left with very few financial options tocope up with their day-to-day affairs. This bill proposes to improve the mannter of computing the monthly pension of retirees by referring to the salary schedule introduced in the Executive Order No. 389 as one of the bases. This bill also aims to change the modes of retirement of those who have retired under RA 1616 and are presently 70 years old or older.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on CIVIL SERVICE AND PROFESSIONAL REGULATION since 2001-08-07

rows.author: C019
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROMOTING SMALL BUSINESS LOCATION AND INCUBATOR PROGRAM
rows.abstract: The proposed measure seels to establish business incubators in strategically viable locations throughout the country, preferably in economic zones or places near academic institutions. Incubators are useful and cost-effective instruments in promoting the survival of new enterprises during their early years of existence by providing a work environment that readily make available business facilities as well as technical and managerial support. Incubators, thus, hasten the transformation of selected, early-stage business with high potential, into self-sufficient , growing and profitable businesses.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on TRADE AND INDUSTRY since 2001-08-07

rows.author: C019
rows.title_full: AN ACT REORGANIZING THE PHILIPPINE STATISTICAL SYSTEM
rows.abstract: The proposed bill aims to (1) ensure the independence of the statistical system to strengthen its credibility; (2) create a Commission that has equal representation from the public and private sectors; (3) respond to information needs of the new millennium; and (4) address the current statistical problems relating to data gaps and inconsistencies , duplication of statistical activities, date reliability, and timeliness and relevance of generated and processed data.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on GOVERNMENT REORGANIZATION since 2001-08-07

rows.author: C102
rows.title_full: AN ACT CREATING THE SUBSIDY OVERSIGHT COUNCIL AND PROVIDING THE RULES FOR A RATIONAL MANAGEMENT OF THE GOVERNMENT SUBSIDY SYSTEM
rows.abstract: Rationale: An important feature of this measure is the creation of the Subsidy Oversight Council as a supervisory and recommendatory commission which will monitor exclusively the grant of tax incentives, government loan guarantees, debt condonation,and concessional loans. All government agencies, which are empowered to grant subsidies, will regularly report on such activities to the Council. The Council shall them summarize such reports and prepare its own Quarterly report to be published in at least six (6) national broad sheets.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on GOVERNMENT REORGANIZATION since 2001-08-07

rows.author: B016
rows.title_full: AN ACT ESTABLISHING A UNIFORM SYSTEM OF RETIREMENT AND SEPARATION BENEFITS FOR THE UNIFORMED PERSONNEL OF THE DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT FURTHER AMENDING REPUBLIC ACT NO. 6975 AS AMENDED BY REPUBLIC ACT NO. 8551 AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: This bill shall cover uniformed personnel of the Department of the Interior and Local Government who are eligible for optional and compulsory retirement and honorable separation from government service. For purposes of this Act, uniformed personnelshall include the uniformed officers and non-officers of the Philippine National Police (PNP), Bureau of Fire Protection (BFP) and Bureau of Jail Managment and Penology (BJMP) organized under R.A. No. 6975.> The proposed bill is a consolidation of various existing laws pertaining to the retirement and separation benefits previously received, extended, granted and entitled to be received by former members of the defunct PC and INP before the creation of PNP, BFP and BJMP.
